executiveSummary: GM1773 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 19,003-person municipality control, 23 neighbourhoods in twelve districts, five BAG places, sixteen BRT settlements, Olst and Wijhe rail stations, 37 scheduled-transit stop areas and five domestic NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 19,015, only twelve above the separately published control (+0.063%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Olst-Wijhe straddles both banks of the IJssel and depends on primary defences, floodplains, regional weteringen, pumps, sewer/wastewater chains, ferries and a narrow north-south road/rail system. The river preset reports 1.714546 inundation stress from T+12 through T+72, 8,465 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 and 699,473.193 deprived person-hours at T+72 without selecting an IJssel hydrograph, one of three contained primary and three contained regional LIWO candidates, a dike/structure state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. The open-coast preset gives zero direct water; retain that narrowly scoped suppression, but do not treat it as an all-clear for northwester IJsselmeer loading, IJssel backwater, weteringen, groundwater, sewer or pluvial pathways. Pluvial reports 0.187849 at T+12/T+24 without the municipality's rain-duration, terrain, sewer, groundwater, pump or receiving-water state. Seven unrelated active hazards reuse the same leading ten neighbourhoods. A controlled T+24 source at the official Buitengebied Den Nul centre near Fortmond/Duursche Waarden produces direct fire 0.567512 and 4,605 affected, yet its containing neighbourhood ranks eighteenth of 23. The static network does not apply the active 24 August–25 December 2026 N337 through-traffic closure, represents neither Olst–Welsum nor Wijhe–Vorchten ferry, and cannot route external 24/7 acute care. Public context identifies 103 water/wastewater objects, local Olst/Wijhe Waterinfo observations, one Enexis planning sample, 43 antenna sites and thirteen education locations, but none establishes complete live topology, flow, backup, staffing or restoration. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, design cases, planned works and static register/schedule status must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1773 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM1773 as Olst-Wijhe in Overijssel and safety region IJsselland and report 19,003 residents, density 167/km², 23.8% aged 65 or older and 2,407 one-person households; the generated centre [6.154171137085497,52.379519370795336] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Twenty-three neighbourhood rows in twelve districts sum to 19,015 residents, twelve above the separately rounded municipality control (+0.063%); households sum to 8,125 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 4,520. Allocation reconciles to the municipality control without rewriting the published rows.

BAG supplies five places—Marle, Olst, Welsum, Wesepe and Wijhe—and BRT supplies sixteen source-labelled settlements: nine woonkernen and seven buurtschappen. No generated place label point falls outside the municipality.

CBS regional statistics expose all 36 fields. District heating and public charging are null in all 23 rows and cars per household is null in two. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; null/suppression remains NoData rather than zero.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — IJsseldijk Zwolle–Olst safety task and current eight-year IJsselwerken programme
evidenceSources.edition: Current project page; official start 17 June 2026; verkenningsrapport 2019
supports: The 29 km primary defence runs from Haereweg in Olst through Wijhe and Herxen to Zwolle and protects Salland/Zwolle from the IJssel and, during northwester storms, from IJsselmeer influence. The authority says it is not strong enough for the future and is being strengthened; that planning statement is not an event-time failure observation.

The strengthening programme officially began 17 June 2026 and is planned for eight years. Work-state, temporary geometry and access can therefore change within the simulator's reference period and require valid-time evidence.

The public verkenningsrapport at https://www.wdodelta.nl/_flysystem/media/verkenningsnrapport-hwbp-ijsseldijk-zwolle-olst.pdf scoped roughly 28.4 km for strengthening and identified four water-retaining structures outside the then-required standard, including RWZI Olst effluent and RWZI Wijhe overflow structures. Historical assessment is not current component condition.
WDODelta provides public planning/project evidence but no blanket machine-reuse licence or incident-time dike, structure, pump or breach-state feed was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 candidate catalogue and current Olst/Wijhe Waterinfo context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; WFS queried 3 September 2026; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: A bounded LIWO WFS query returns five primary and four regional candidates; point-in-polygon against the generated boundary contains primary Olst, Wijhe and Windesheim plus regional Meenhorst, Wijhe Oost and Wijhe West. Bbox-only candidates outside the polygon were not assigned.

Candidate points and frequency-class flags are scenario-selection metadata, not active failures, forecasts, connected inundation footprints or metre depths. Operational use must pin release, water boundary/datum, defence/control state, footprint, arrival, depth/velocity, duration/recession, units, CRS/resolution, uncertainty, coverage, NoData, licence and authority approval.

The cached observations contain Olst discharge 143.64 m³/s and water level 27 cm NAP plus Wijhe water level 7 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026. Forecasts cover requested T+1/T+6/T+12/T+24 only; no T+48/T+72 feature exists.

Waterinfo values are observation/forecast context with distinct issue and valid times, parameter, datum and quality; they are not the canonical exercise hydrograph. Waterinfo is CC0/non-mission-critical. Missing horizons remain NoData, not zero water or safe conditions.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Climate-adaptation policy, programme and municipal sewer/groundwater duties
evidenceSources.edition: Climate policy adopted 2 March 2026; implementation programme adopted 17 March 2026 for 2026–2028; GRP 2022–2028
supports: The municipality adopted its Climate Adaptation Policy on 2 March 2026 and a 2026–2028 implementation programme on 17 March 2026. These documents establish current planning and governance, not an observed event or completed measure.

The municipal sewer plan at https://www.olst-wijhe.nl/ondernemers/bedrijventerreinen/bedrijventerrein-de-meente-noord/bijlagen-kavelverkoop-bedrijventerrein-de-meente-noord/bijlagen-kavelverkoop-bedrijventerrein-de-meente-noord/kaderstellende-documenten/gemeentelijke-rioleringsplan-olst-wijhe-2022-2028.pdf distinguishes wastewater, rainwater and groundwater duties, identifies water nuisance, heat, drought and flood stress tests, and states rural pressure sewers are not designed for rainwater.

The plan calls for monitoring groundwater, addressing both high levels and summer deficits, surface retention/storage before discharge, masterplans for settlement rainwater and fewer combined-sewer overflows. These are distinct causal pathways that a single municipal pluvial scalar cannot represent.

The municipal documents are public administrative evidence; no standard redistribution licence, machine API, native stress-test resolution or guaranteed update cadence was identified on the cited pages.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Active N337 restriction, emergency access and ferry dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current works page valid 24 August–25 December 2026; municipal FAQ inspected 3 September 2026
supports: At audit time the N337 between Olst and Den Nul is closed to through traffic from 24 August until 25 December 2026. Residents, cycles, emergency services and bus 161 may use the parallel road; extra travel time and pressure on diversion routes are explicitly expected.
A further De Kneu–De Meente closure is announced for October/November but its exact planning and diversion were not yet published. Future unspecified restriction details remain Unknown until valid.

The municipal FAQ at https://www.olst-wijhe.nl/samenleven/werken-aan-de-ijsseldijk/veelgestelde-vragen-afsluiting-n337/veelgestelde-vragen-over-afsluiting-n337 says Olst and Wijhe ferries are intended to continue during the works, but low water can prevent sailing and an undated Veerweg junction weekend closure will require an Abbott-site diversion.

The municipality's August 2026 ferry-card decision says about 280 Welsum/Marle households rely on the ferries for care, social activity and municipal services. This is dependency evidence, not incident-time ferry operation or passenger capacity. No blanket reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Duursche Waarden, Fortmond woodland and visitor-access context
supports: Staatsbosbeheer identifies Fortmond in Olst and a 2.5 km path through dense floodplain forest in the Duursche Waarden, with visitor parking, monument and lookout tower. The municipality also describes the area as a water-rich marsh/nature visitor destination on the IJssel.

Official context establishes combustible woodland/vegetation and transient visitation eligibility near Den Nul/Fortmond, but not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, access, extinguishing-water availability, suppression or occupancy.
The controlled audit source uses an official neighbourhood centre to test source containment; it is synthetic and not a live incident or forecast.
No machine-readable local fire perimeter, visitor counter, operational cadence or standard reuse licence was identified on these pages.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — External acute care, rail, scheduled transit and domestic road context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail snapshot and GTFS v9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026
supports: RIVM acute-care v1.1 is CC0 static survey data. It assigns no respondent acute-care point inside GM1773; nearest to the municipal centre are 24/7 Deventer Ziekenhuis at 13.37 km and Isala Zwolle at 15.03 km, both reporting acute obstetrics. Distance is not an ambulance route or live acceptance state.

NWB supplies five logical links but only three physical corridor identities: N756 toward Raalte, N348 toward Raalte and Deventer, and N337 toward Zwolle and Deventer. Each 150 scenario-unit route is Mobility/Supply-only; paired edges on N348/N337 are series continuations, not additive emergency capacity.

ProRail supplies stations Olst and Wijhe and GTFS assigns 37 stop areas. Static station/stop geometry and feed-valid schedules do not establish passengers, accessibility, rolling stock, emergency role or actual operation.

The graph contains no ferry/cross-IJssel edge to the west bank and no destination-level ambulance/care route. NWB is CC0; RIVM is CC0; source/version/feed validity must remain attached to rail and transit context.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / WDODelta / Netbeheer Nederland / Enexis / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water, wastewater, electricity, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; authority project pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Generated containment assigns 103 HWH points: eight sewer pumps, eighteen surface-water pumps, one wastewater treatment plant and 76 weirs. HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial, weekly where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0; register presence/capacity is not connectivity, telemetry, live operation, backup or restoration.

WDODelta documents a pressure main carrying Wijhe wastewater to RWZI Olst, rerouted because part lay in the IJsseldijk, and names RWZI Olst and Wijhe sewer pump. Planned June 2025 commissioning is not proof of current topology/condition or exercise-time operation.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Enexis OL Olst and reports 43.2 MW existing withdrawal, 21.6 MW required withdrawal, 3.0 MW/eight-request withdrawal queue, 43.2 MW existing injection, 49.7 MW required injection and 52.8 MW/eight-request injection queue with twelve projects and earliest year 2026. This is planning capacity, not live load/outage/switching/reserve; exact reuse licence was not identified.

RDI assigns 43 antenna sites—eighteen mobile, sixteen fixed-link, eight amateur and one broadcast—and DUO assigns thirteen education uses—six primary, one secondary and six other. RDI register terms/cadence are not a live coverage contract; DUO RIO is daily attribution-licensed register data. Points do not establish connectivity, occupancy, shelter role or operation.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Current regional crisis-plan and response-governance context
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2023–2026 and strategic policy agenda 2023–2026 listed as current on 3 September 2026
supports: The safety region's current documentation says its 2023–2026 crisis plan defines the crisis organisation, information lines and roles/responsibilities, while the strategic agenda governs current ambitions. This is organisational planning evidence, not activation or performance in a particular incident.

Public plan availability does not establish warning receipt, dike inspection, ferry/road/rail status, evacuation, shelter, care acceptance, water-chain control, resupply, dewatering or restoration at any simulator checkpoint.

The public knowledge platform notes that current plans/procedures are maintained in the regional handbook. Public pages do not provide a complete machine action/resource/decision-state feed or guaranteed update cadence.
No standard redistribution licence was identified; public plan text may support governance labels but not exact operational resource counts or execution claims.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, ferry/road/rail operating decision, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude ferry passengers, commuters, pupils, patients, staff, nature/event visitors, responders and displaced people; no timestamped dynamic occupancy is consumed.

Generalized administrative polygons and centroids cannot resolve IJssel floodplains/compartments, dike/structure state, wetering/pump/sewer/groundwater catchments, combustible vegetation, ferry landings or utility zones.

Six contained LIWO points are candidates, not breaches or footprints. Bbox queries include outside points unless polygon-filtered, and candidate frequency flags are not current probability, water level, depth or arrival.
Waterinfo observations/forecasts are valid-time public context and stop at requested T+24 in the cache. They are not selected as the exercise hydrograph and missing T+48/T+72 is NoData.

Future-standard dike non-compliance and an eight-year strengthening programme do not mean event-time failure. Construction status, temporary defences and component condition can change and remain Unknown without a valid feed.
Municipal climate policy, GRP and stress-test references establish responsibilities and planning, not a live rain event, groundwater field, sewer/pump state, completed measure or local depth.

The controlled nature-fire source is synthetic. Official vegetation/visitor context does not establish current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, occupancy, access, extinguishing water, crew or suppression.

NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static/register/schedule evidence. The N337 page gives a current restriction but not live diversion throughput; future subphase timing is pending and ferries can change with water/operations.

RIVM's zero internal acute-care respondent points does not erase local care or demand. Centre distance to Deventer/Isala is not route time, ambulance availability, live acceptance, beds, staff, utilities or backup.

HWH coverage is partial/provider-dependent. Registered object, type or capacity does not establish connected topology, current operation, compatible flow units, power/backup, control sequence or recovery.

One NBNL postcode sample, RDI antennas, DUO schools and absent local air/weather points are planning/register/coverage context. They do not establish customer connectivity, occupancy, load, signal, air surface, outage, reserve or repair.

Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply, ferry and emergency-resource topology/live state may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic/derived screening until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
